also: tell the cook it was delicious
give my compliments to the cook

evidence: Cic. Att. 16.11.8: Atticae … meīs verbīs suāvium dēs volō
terms.comment: Our sentence, built on Cicero’s meīs verbīs, “in my name, from me”, which he uses for messages passed on through someone else. We have found no set phrase for praising the cook in Petronius’s dinner, Horace’s dinner satires, Terence, or Traupman; the authors praise a dish, or the master rewards the cook (see the examples). For the head cook of a restaurant, see “chef”.

phrases.latin: Optimē cēnāvimus; coquum meīs verbīs laudā.
phrases.english: That was a wonderful dinner; give the cook our compliments.
Tell the cook the fish was delicious.

phrases.latin: Hoc salsum est; hoc adustum est; hoc lautum est parum; illud rēctē: iterum sīc mementō.
phrases.english: This one’s too salty; this one’s burnt; this one isn’t washed enough; that one’s right: remember to do it that way again.

phrases.latin: Nec nōn cocus pōtiōne honōrātus est.
phrases.english: And the cook too was honoured with a drink.

sources: Lewis & Short: coquus · Lewis & Short: laudo
